title: Jinnsart Style (MOSS-Image) [LORA/MOSS Image]
description:
Model trained on base MOSS-Image (int8) to imitate the style of Jinnsart

=====

General note on MOSS-Image: Through the personal testing I've done and what I've seen from others: MOSS is not the ideal candidate for anime style LORAs as of right now, especially compared to a model like Anima. But, it is an extremely powerful model, and I've seen the style LORAs are in demand and do serve some purpose, so I will still gladly train them (especially for some of my Anima favorites). If what I hear of MOSS releasing an anime-centric version of the model someday is true, I'll be retraining a lot of these models in the future. For now, try adding things to the prompt to help describe the art style (e.g. 'glossy anime style illustration' or 'Illustration in a cartoon style with flat bold colors and thick black outlines', etc.), use higher weights, or other more precise prompting methods.

NOTE: All the images I generate for the showcase are done with base MOSS-Image

title: FromSoftware Concept Art (Dark Souls / Elden Ring) [LORA/Anima]
description:
A unified FromSoftware Concept Art style LoRA trained on 118 curated official concept paintings from Dark Souls 1–3 Design Works and Elden Ring Official Art Books (characters, bosses, armor, and monumental environments).

Designed to transfer gritty Design Works brushwork, weathered metal textures, tattered cloth, and moody gothic/golden-hour atmosphere onto both dark fantasy subjects and out-of-domain scenes (like sci-fi).

Trigger Word & Recommended Weights

Trigger Word: fs_concept

Illustrious XL (v1.0): 0.8 – 1.2 (1.0 sweet spot; Clip Skip 2)

MOSS-Image (v1.1): 0.8 – 1.2 (1.0 sweet spot; Euler, CFG 3.0; trained on MOSS-Image Base and tested on SFT)

Krea 2 (v1.1): 0.8 – 1.2 (1.0 sweet spot; upgraded dataset labeling for much stronger painterly style transfer than v1.0, holds cleanly up to 1.2)

Anima (v1.1): 0.8 – 1.2 (1.0 sweet spot; Euler / Euler a / er_sde, 25–30 steps, CFG 4.0–5.0; trained on Anima Base and tested on WAI-ANIMA;

title: NegBeta Dual3 IL - Toward WAI, Away from NoobAI (Illustrious) [Checkpoint/Illustrious]
description:
NegBeta Dual3 IL - Toward WAI, Away from NoobAI (Illustrious) adds WAI finish and removes NoobAI paint, the cleanest line-quality variant in the batch.

[Recipe] Two stacked differences on UNet only: Nova Anime XL IL v19.0 + 0.25 x (WAI-illustrious IL v1.0 - Nova Anime XL IL v19.0) + -0.12 x (NoobAI-XL EPS Four-Mix (CyberFix) - Nova Anime XL IL v19.0). VAE and text encoders inherited from Nova Anime XL IL v19.0.

title: Anytime-Valid Sequential Verification for Sensing-Efficient Robot Navigation under Perception Uncertainty
description: When a robot navigates an unfamiliar grid, noisy sensor readings can make it hard to tell whether the cells along its next move are free. Additional scans can reduce that uncertainty, but a fixed scan count spends the same sensing effort at every position. In a static-grid simulation, a sequential rule uses a Gaussian likelihood ratio to determine when the cells newly covered by the robot's footprint have enough evidence of free space. On 324 held-out scenarios from 18 public maps, the sequential gate and a four-scan reference chosen on validation data both completed every mission without an observed collision. With their respective validation-selected routing weights, the gate averaged 123.15 scans per episode versus 224.13 for the reference, a reduction of 45.05% (95% map-stratified bootstrap interval: 42.21--48.95%). In a retrospective check on the same scenarios with routing weights held equal, the reductions were 43.91% and 43.37% at the two tested weights, with all missions completed. On 216 scenarios from 12 previously unused maps, allocating more of the same certification error budget near the initial start--goal rectangle cut the sequential gate's scan count by a further 11.58%. The spatial variant completed 206 missions versus 208 for the original gate and increased computation time. The collision bound depends on the assumed observation model and footprint geometry. In a stress test with persistent per-cell bias, the original gate completed 0 of 54 missions.

title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
description: Post-training large language models (LLMs) for mathematical reasoning often relies on accepted traces whose final answers pass a verifier. For hard math problems, however, such traces can be rare under independent Monte Carlo (MC) sampling. To address this, we propose Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces (DART), a trace-mining method that starts from a rejected trace, decomposes it into reasoning steps, and ranks them by position-weighted uncertainty. It then generates deliberately distinct alternative candidates for highly ranked steps using reference-answer guidance and a meta-thought before completing the resulting traces. On greedy-unsolved DeepMath-103K problems, DART recovers 37% more problems than MC sampling at a matched number of generated traces. Its estimated generation cost per recovered problem is nearly identical, while its cost per accepted trace is 30% lower. Post-training Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on traces mined by DART achieves the highest point estimate in five of six evaluations across MATH-500 and AIME benchmarks. These results demonstrate that revisiting rejected traces with DART can expand problem coverage and provide effective post-training data.

title: VulnSafe: Measuring Vulnerability-Aware Relational Safety in Large Language Models
description: Emotionally supportive interactions require large language models not only to avoid overtly harmful content, but also to recognize vulnerability-related risk, regulate their relational stance, preserve user agency, and provide context-appropriate support. Following an evidence-centered design, 41 scenarios elicit construct-relevant behavior through 2,050 balanced prompts and scenario-specific scoring rubrics. The assessment further separates proactive should-do behavior from prohibitive should-not behavior. Across eight representative LLMs, results show distinct competence profiles and larger disparities than prohibitive requirements. VulnSafe therefore makes relational safety interpretable as a multidimensional model capability rather than as refusal compliance alone.

title: EPPC-CARE: Staged Hierarchical Annotation of Communication Behaviors in Secure Patient-Provider Messages
description: Objectives: Patient portal messages provide invaluable information about communication dynamics between patients and healthcare providers, but extracting it manually is labor-intensive. We developed and evaluated EPPC-CARE, an automated framework for identifying communication behaviors together with the supporting text for each classification. Materials and Methods: From 867 messages, we obtained 5,516 reference standard annotations. Each annotation is a triplet of communication-related text (span), a broader communication category (Code), and a specific subcategory (Sub-code). We evaluated EPPC-CARE's identified triplets across six open-weight large language models (LLMs) against supervised fine-tuning and communication-based models such as EPPC-OASIS. We also compared EPPC-CARE with human expert annotations on 100 messages. Results: EPPC-CARE improved performance over EPPC-OASIS across all six models. EPPC-CARE's Triplet F1 improved by 2.90 percentage points on average, with a best score of 64.4%. On the human expert evaluation subset, EPPC-CARE and the human expert showed comparable agreement with the reference standard, with differences favoring EPPC-CARE. Discussion: These findings suggest that identifying triplet components (span, code, subcode) sequentially can improve performance across model families while preserving the supporting text behind each identification.
